[1] TLS.md (LAN HTTP (no TLS))
  Enable HTTP/2 on your reverse proxy: Whichever reverse proxy you use, make sure it serves SilverBullet over HTTP/2. Over HTTP/1.1, browsers allow only six simultaneous connections per host, and SilverBullet’s service worker and sync engine can use all of them. When that happens, every request stalls: the client reports “Could not reach remote server, we’re offline or the server is down”, requests to `/.ping` time out, and pages load slowly from the local copy, even though the server itself is up. / * **Caddy** enables HTTP/2 by default, so the configuration above needs no changes. / * **nginx**: add `http2 on;` to the `server` block (nginx 1.25.1 and later), or use `listen 443 ssl http2;` on older versions. / * **Nginx Proxy Manager**: edit the proxy host, open the _SSL_ tab and enable _HTTP/2 Support_. / To check, run the following, which should print `2`: / ```shell
  Don’t buffer the event stream: SilverBullet keeps a server-sent events stream open at `/.events` for live updates. The server sends a ping on it every 30 seconds. If your reverse proxy buffers or compresses this stream, those pings never reach the browser. Live updates then fall back to polling, and stale streams can pile up in the browser and hold connections open. / * **Caddy** passes event streams through unbuffered, so the configuration above needs no changes. [2] CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG)
  Edge: * [[MCP]]: SilverBullet Server can now serve an MCP endpoint at `/.mcp`, so AI assistants can directly read, write, search and query your spaces. Clients sign in with OAuth and act as the account that approved them, on the spaces chosen on a consent page. MCP is off by default: an admin turns it on in the APIs tab. / * **Potentially breaking:** the legacy `/.auth/authorize` and `/.auth/token` endpoints now only accept SilverBullet’s own clients (`silverbullet-app`, `silverbullet-cli` and `silverbullet-share`); other `client_id`s are refused. / * Fix: slow filesystem watcher registration no longer delays space startup. Polling tracks changes while native notifications start, and a resync reconciles changes made during registration.
[3] CLI.md (Installation)
  > **note** This is **not** the server / > `sb` is the optional **CLI client**, it talks to an already-running SilverBullet instance over HTTP. If you’re looking for the actual server binary, that’s [[Install/Server Binary]] (`silverbullet`), not this. You do not need `sb` to use SilverBullet. / The SilverBullet CLI is a companion command-line tool for interacting with a running SilverBullet instance from your terminal. It communicates with the server over HTTP. File commands use the [[HTTP API]] directly. Lua, queries, screenshots and logs use the [[Runtime API]]. `sb help` gives an AI assistant or a person the space’s skills and a map of the space (see [[#`help [topic]`]]).
Exact facts:
- [1] Open your server using its LAN address, for example `http://192.168.1.20:3000`. The server must listen on an address reachable from your LAN. Editing, indexing, queries, Space Lua, plugs, attachments, and local password login remain available.
- [1] If you run SilverBullet _locally_ on your machine, this is the easiest option. Everything runs fine as long as the browser sees `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` appear in the URL, even with `http://`.
